questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you about an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road, if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Tell the other driver who you are. Offer help if needed.

questions.question: You should be cautious when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid objects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid objects on the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may suddenly swerve to avoid objects on the road. Always be careful when driving near bicycles.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and watch carefully. Look both ways for traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic light, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A fully loaded truck traveling at 55 mph may take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded truck may need about 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is near.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns from green to solid yellow, you should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and go through the intersection.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
Speed up to go through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means slow down and stop before entering the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
Look for another train on the other track after the first train passes.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for another train on the other track after the first train passes.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks, a second train may be on the other track. Wait and look both ways on both tracks before crossing. Make sure no train is coming from any direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm pointing upward means they are turning right. If you see this signal, adjust your driving based on their turn.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you just came from.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following should drivers NOT do?

options.text: Dim their headlights when within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Use their parking lights only while parked.
Dim their headlights when following within 200 feet of another vehicle.
Avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights by glancing toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dim their headlights when within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.explanation: Dim your headlights when within 500 feet of oncoming traffic and when following within 200 feet of another vehicle. Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded. Use parking lights only when parked.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Why should you be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are more difficult to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more difficult to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can be hidden in a car's blind spot. It may be hard to judge distance to a motorcycle or tell how fast it is moving. Always be alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is controlling traffic ahead in a construction area.

questions.question: How should railroad crossings always be considered?

options.text: Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.
Dangerous.
Safe locations to park a car.
A place where it is required to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flagger instructions. Only cross when you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: When parked facing downhill, where should your front wheels be turned?

options.text: Aiming straight ahead.
Turned toward the curb.
Turned away from the curb.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turned toward the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the curb when parked downhill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What should drivers do when they see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should come to a complete stop.
May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns in the direction of the arrow. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians because they have a green light.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When another car is on your left and you both reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians who are on the sidewalk.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination more quickly.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the space between your car and the car in front of you.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is ahead.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line along the road edge marks the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. If the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
You can only pass in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.
